items.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia
items.description: Amazon has ditched its plans to build four new data centers in Loudoun County, Northern Virginia, following an outcry from local residents and officials. The land will now be repurposed for mixed and residential use.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Amazon will no longer build four new data centers on the site of the George Washington University's campus in Loudoun County, just outside of D.C., and will instead repurpose the majority of the 122-acre space for mixed-use and residential development following significant pushback from the local community. It will also donate 25 acres of the property to Loudoun County to be used for a community arts center and new recreational facility. On top of all that, it'll even give $5 million to the county's fund for housing, reports The Washington Post.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedThat's quite the turnaround compared to plans to build in a county that is already dubbed "Data Center Alley" because it has the largest concentration of data centers on the planet. But residents' concerns about the noise generated by such data centers and the incredible amount of power that they require to function have seen the county's approach to new data center buildouts change of late. Amazon first submitted its proposal to build the new facilities in July, and Loudoun County Board of Supervisors Chair Phyllis J. Randall and Amazon met in September, where it was put to the company that it may be better to find an alternative use for the land.Josh Weissman, Amazon’s vice president in charge of data center development, said the company had jumped at the chance to purchase the former university campus when the opportunity arose, but added that the company considered the county’s “pointed concerns about data center development at this particular site.” Weissman added that “While we see the property’s legal development potential differently than the County does, we concluded that the best outcome for all is to come together on a shared vision for this campus rather than engage in costly litigation.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The building of new data centers has always been a necessity given our growing use of cloud-based services and storage systems. But the recent boom in AI use has seen demand for additional, and larger, facilities ratcheted up to new levels. But with that demand comes opposition, with local communities wary of the impact these mammoth facilities can have on the areas in which they live, including spikes in the price of electricity. Officials have begun taking steps to try to grease the wheels of data center construction. Just days before this news broke, President Donald Trump called for data center builders and AI hyperscalers to pay local communities a dividend amid energy-related price increases. In a social media post, Trump went on to say that data centers would be required not only to make their own electricity but also to give or sell excess energy back to the local community. Water shortages and deforestation have also become key issues affecting the communities in which data centers are being placed.Back in Loudoun County, officials pointed to what could be achieved when choosing dialog over confrontation. “By choosing dialogue over reflexive disagreement, Loudoun County and Amazon created an opportunity for the County,” Randall reportedly said via statement. “This agreement provides new places for our Loudoun residents to gather, create, and play. And, most importantly to me, we will provide more attainable homes for working families.” You may like Virginia county with 250 data centers begins to rein in building Amazon warns $68 billion in blocked data centers threatens US AI lead AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin quickly blocking new developments Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors

items.titleZh: 亚马逊迫于当地对AI数据中心的反对，放弃在北弗吉尼亚新建四座设施的计划
items.descriptionZh:
亚马逊已决定不再在乔治·华盛顿大学位于弗吉尼亚州劳登县、华盛顿特区近郊的校园地块上建设四座新数据中心，而是将122英亩土地的大部分改作混合用途和住宅开发。这一转向发生在地当地社区强烈反对之后。亚马逊还将向劳登县捐赠25英亩土地，用于建设社区艺术中心和新的休闲设施，并向该县住房基金捐款500万美元。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，这与此前在“数据中心巷”继续扩张的计划形成明显反差——劳登县因拥有全球最大规模的数据中心集群而被称为“数据中心巷”，但居民对数据中心噪音和巨大耗电量的担忧，已促使该县对新数据中心建设采取更审慎态度。

事件时间线显示，亚马逊于7月首次提交建设新数据中心的提案，9月与劳登县监事会主席菲利斯·J·兰德尔会面，县方提出为该地块寻找替代用途可能更合适。亚马逊数据中心开发副总裁乔什·韦斯曼表示，公司当初抓住机会购买这处前大学校园地块，但也考虑了县方对“这一特定地点数据中心开发”的尖锐关切。他说，尽管亚马逊与县方对该地块的法律开发潜力看法不同，但公司认为共同形成校园愿景比陷入代价高昂的诉讼更符合各方利益。

从技术需求背景看，云服务和存储系统持续增长，使新建数据中心长期具有必要性；而近期AI应用爆发进一步推高了对更大规模设施的需求。数据中心为AI训练、推理和云服务提供算力、存储与网络，需要持续供电和冷却，并产生噪音，因此其选址越来越受电力、水资源和社区承受能力约束。原文未披露这四座数据中心原计划的IT负载、PUE、用水量等具体性能参数，但协议中的关键“参数”包括：不再建设四座数据中心、122英亩地块大部分改为混合用途和住宅、捐赠25英亩公共设施用地、500万美元住房基金。这反映出数据中心开发模式的一种调整：不再只强调土地和法律开发权，而是通过土地捐赠、住房基金和公共设施等社区收益包换取社会许可，并以协商替代诉讼。

围绕数据中心的反对还涉及电价上涨、水资源短缺和森林砍伐等问题。就在这一消息传出前几天，美国总统特朗普呼吁数据中心建设者和AI超大规模企业向当地社区支付“红利”，并要求数据中心自行发电，并将多余电力赠送或出售给当地社区。劳登县官员则强调对话优于对抗。兰德尔表示，通过选择对话而非条件反射式反对，劳登县和亚马逊为该县创造了机会；协议将为居民提供聚会、创作和活动的场所，更重要的是为工薪家庭提供更多可负担住房。

这一案例的技术影响不在芯片或服务器本身，而在AI基础设施扩张的落地方式：随着AI数据中心功率密度和总用电规模上升，项目能否推进越来越取决于电力配套、噪音控制、用水约束和社区利益共享。未来超大规模数据中心选址可能更早引入社区沟通，并配套自发电、余电回馈、公共设施和住房基金等机制。应用场景上，这既关系到亚马逊云服务和AI算力的长期扩容，也为地方政府与数据中心运营商处理选址冲突提供了一个“协商换社区收益”的样本。

items.title: Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network
items.description: A security firm has been able to identify 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 AI chips running inside a China Telecom network, but it's unclear where the export-barred components are physically located.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Lava, an Israeli security firm, says that it has been able to identify 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips within the network of China Telecom, a state-owned company that provides telecommunications services within the country. These same chips have already been barred from export by U.S. export controls, a report by The Information notes, which begs the question of how they have turned up in a Chinese data center. Such chips can only be sold to whitelisted buyers who agree not to export them to sanctioned parties, including those in China.However, banning companies from buying Nvidia's high-performance GPUs and AI data center chips hasn't always worked. In 2025, it was reported that Chinese companies smuggled $1 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips into the country in three months. At the time, the B200 chips were the most sought-after, but some distributors were already gearing up to sell B300-series chips when they became available.While the latest finding shows that the proliferation of export-controlled chips into China continues to be an issue, Nvidia has downplayed the report but didn't deny the findings. "Governments, researchers, and media have all found insignificant diversion of controlled US products, less than one half of one percent in recent court cases — a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has," an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. "With tens of millions of GPUs in service in approved countries, this report again demonstrates that smuggling is a nonfactor, blocked by governments on both sides of the globe."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: It's unknown how B300 chips found their way into China Telecom's server racks, nor can Lava confirm exactly where within the company's network they are located. But they are there, with Lava identifying them via Nvidia's own DCGM Exporter tool. The software can be installed by data center operators and is used to monitor server health and performance, and while designed for internal use, it can oftentimes be accessed beyond the data center's network. Oddly, it doesn't always require password authentication, either. Nvidia previously confirmed it was working on a tool that would allow its chips to be located, but it is yet to be released.It's easy to see why Chinese firms are keen to get their hands on the Blackwell Ultra B300. Announced in March of last year, the data center GPU is one of the most powerful on the planet, offering huge performance gains with 50% more memory and FP4 compute than the previous-generation B200. At the time, Nvidia touted that the chip was "built for the age of reasoning," while name-checking more sophisticated AI LLMs like DeepSeek R1. At the time of its announcement, the B300 was expected to ship by the end of 2025, and it didn't take long for it to become hot property. In August 2026, nine people were indicted in Taiwan over the illegal export of B300 GPUs to China. This came just days after Supermicro confirmed that it had fired several employees following an investigation into smuggling. The complicated smuggling process included the use of a Taiwanese server trading firm called Flying Tiget Tech — a firm with whitelisted status for GPU purchases. You may like Nvidia employee implicated in escalating AI GPU smuggling scandal Nine indicted by Taiwan over illegal export of Nvidia B300 GPUs to China — details reveal five-point strategy to exploit and avoid customs controls Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Nvidia's chips have proven so vital to AI data centers that demand for even its older silicon has caused skyrocketing prices. The company's A100 servers have tripled in price, despite being five years old, and can cost up to $82.,000. The ongoing crackdown on Nvidia chip smuggling has even seen some resort to retooling gaming GPUs to run AI workloads where possible. items.titleZh: 国有中国电信网络中发现非法英伟达Blackwell Ultra B300 GPU
items.descriptionZh:
以色列安全公司Lava称，其在中国电信的网络中识别出32颗英伟达Blackwell Ultra B300数据中心GPU。中国电信是中国国有电信服务提供商，而这些B300芯片属于美国出口管制禁止对华出口的高性能AI芯片。The Information报道称，这一发现引出了关键问题：受控芯片如何进入中国数据中心。按照美国管制规则，此类芯片只能出售给白名单买家，且买家须承诺不将其再出口至受制裁方，包括中国实体。英伟达方面淡化报告影响，但未否认Lava的发现。其发言人表示，政府、研究机构和媒体近期在法院案件中发现的受控美国产品转移“微不足道”，不到0.5%，相比中国已拥有的海量本土算力只是“沧海一粟”；在获批国家有数千万颗GPU在役，报告再次说明走私并非主要因素，且受到全球多国政府拦截。

Lava并未说明这些B300如何进入中国电信的服务器机架，也无法确认它们在中国电信网络中的具体位置，但表示芯片确实存在。识别方式是利用英伟达自有的DCGM Exporter工具。该软件由数据中心运营商安装，用于监控服务器健康状态和性能，原本面向内部使用，但经常可从数据中心网络外部访问，而且并不总是要求密码认证。英伟达此前确认正在开发一种可定位其芯片的工具，但尚未发布。这一发现也暴露了AI数据中心监控接口暴露带来的硬件部署信息泄露风险。

中国公司之所以热衷获取Blackwell Ultra B300，是因为该数据中心GPU是当前最强性能产品之一。它于去年3月发布，英伟达称其“为推理时代而构建”，并点名DeepSeek R1等更复杂的AI大模型。与上一代B200相比，B300的内存容量和FP4计算能力均提升50%。FP4是一种低精度浮点格式，可在AI推理中降低内存带宽和能耗、提高吞吐量；更大的内存则有助于承载更大模型、减少多卡通信开销。B300原预计2025年底出货，随后迅速成为抢手货。2026年8月，台湾九人因非法向中国出口B300 GPU被起诉；几天前，Supermicro在走私调查后确认解雇数名员工。报道称，复杂走私链条涉及一家名为Flying Tiget Tech的台湾服务器贸易公司，该公司拥有GPU采购白名单资格。

这一事件延续了受出口管制英伟达AI芯片持续流入中国的背景。2025年曾有报道称，中国公司在三个月内走私了价值10亿美元的英伟达AI芯片，当时B200最受欢迎，部分分销商已准备在B300上市后销售。英伟达芯片对AI数据中心至关重要，甚至旧款产品价格也大幅上涨：发布五年的A100服务器价格已上涨两倍，最高可达8.2万美元；在走私打击持续之际，还有人尝试改造游戏GPU用于AI工作负载。总体来看，B300现身中国电信网络说明，尽管美国出口管制和白名单机制已建立，但通过分销链、服务器集成和跨境贸易规避管制的风险仍然存在；同时，DCGM Exporter等运维工具的外部暴露也为追踪受控硬件提供了线索。该事件将影响美国出口管制有效性辩论、英伟达合规与供应链审查，以及运营商AI数据中心的安全配置实践。B300的主要应用场景包括大规模AI推理、运营商AI云服务和数据中心大模型部署。

items.title: FCC issues first bans under new chip-level rule
items.description: FCC bans a dashcam and wireless video transmitter produced by HiSilicon, a subsidiary of Huawei for containing an AI chip that advertises face detection algorithms.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The FCC recently imposed a new rule allowing it to ban devices based on the internal chips instead of basing bans on individual products or brands, thus closing the loophole of rebranded products with parts from Chinese manufacturers on US export restriction lists. Using this new rule, the FCC has banned two devices from being sold and marketed in the US for the first time: a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter. As reported by The Verge, these devices were banned due to the HiSilicon Smart Vision SoC (System on a Chip) they contain, which features built-in detection algorithms for faces. HiSilicon is a subsidiary of Huawei, and the firm and its subsidiaries are on the FCC’s Covered List of entities that pose a risk to US national security.The Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision is an SoC for surveillance and camera products. The SoC is meant to be used for things like vehicle dashcams and wireless CCTV systems; fully equipped with WiFi, Ethernet, video encoding chips, an Arm Cortex-A7, and an NPU (Neural Processing Unit) for AI features. The NPU is what the FCC is concerned about, explaining that it is a device that contains logic-bearing “smart” components produced by entities on the Covered List. (Image credit: HiSilicon)On the SoC’s data sheet, the Intelligent Video Engine (IVE) uses the NPU that runs a built-in dedicated multimodal large model and transformer feature acceleration. The transformer feature acceleration allows the AI model to understand the relationship between objects from one video frame to another, keeping “attention” between related objects: pets, faces, human figures, and parcels, as the data sheet advertises. For consumers, this potentially means the AI in a surveillance camera can understand whether it is your pet that is escaping, or an unknown person is stealing your parcel after understanding that it was placed by a courier worker.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, the FCC believes the logic-bearing AI in the SoC can do something much more nefarious, surveying US citizens and logging faces for foreign surveillance. Huawei already had a previous AI chip scandal, using shell companies to deceive TSMC into producing AI chips for them, going against the US’ request for TSMC to halt supplies to a list of Chinese customers; among other Huawei scandals leading to other product bans in the US. items.titleZh: FCC依据新芯片级规则首次发布禁令
items.descriptionZh:
美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）近期实施了一项新的设备准入规则，使其可以依据设备内部所用芯片，而非仅依据具体产品型号或品牌，来决定是否禁止相关设备进入美国市场。这一规则改变了此前监管主要针对整机产品或品牌的路径，重点堵住“重新贴牌”规避限制的漏洞：即使最终产品以不同品牌销售，只要其中包含来自美国出口限制名单或FCC“ Covered List”上中国厂商的部件，FCC仍可对设备实施禁售。借助这一新规，FCC首次禁止两款设备在美国销售和推广：一款行车记录仪和一款无线视频传输器。据The Verge报道，这两款产品被禁的原因是其内部使用了海思（HiSilicon）的Smart Vision系统级芯片（SoC），该芯片内置人脸检测算法。海思是华为子公司，而华为及其子公司被列入FCC的“Covered List”，该名单涵盖被认定对美国国家安全构成风险的实体。

涉事芯片型号为Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision，定位面向监控和摄像类产品的SoC，目标应用包括车载行车记录仪和无线CCTV系统。该芯片集成WiFi、以太网、视频编码芯片、Arm Cortex-A7 CPU，以及用于AI功能的NPU（神经网络处理单元）。FCC主要担忧的正是其NPU及由此带来的“智能”逻辑处理能力。FCC解释称，这类设备包含由“Covered List”实体生产的、具备逻辑运算能力的智能组件。

根据该SoC的数据表，其智能视频引擎（IVE）利用NPU运行内置的专用多模态大模型，并支持Transformer特征加速。Transformer特征加速使AI模型能够理解不同视频帧中对象之间的关系，并在相关对象之间保持“注意力”，数据表宣传的对象包括宠物、人脸、人体和包裹。对消费者而言，这意味着监控摄像头中的AI有望区分具体场景：例如，是自家的宠物正在跑出去，还是陌生人正在偷走包裹，并且能够理解包裹是由快递员放置的。这类边缘AI视觉能力可提升车载记录、家庭和商业安防、无线视频传输等场景的智能分析体验。

不过，FCC认为，该SoC中具备逻辑运算能力的AI还可能被用于更敏感的目的，例如对美国公民进行监控、记录人脸信息并用于外国 surveillance。报道还提到，华为此前曾卷入AI芯片相关丑闻，被指利用空壳公司欺骗台积电为其生产AI芯片，违反美国要求台积电停止向一批中国客户供货的要求；此外还有其他华为相关事件导致其产品在美国被禁。需要指出的是，原文并未披露该芯片的具体算力、功耗、视频帧率、检测精度等量化性能参数，也没有给出与其他同类芯片的逐项对比数据。此次事件更重要的“对比”在于监管方式的变化：从此前针对具体产品/品牌的禁令，转向可依据内部芯片实施禁售，并且这是FCC首次依据该规则禁止设备。其影响可能延伸到美国市场的安防摄像头、行车记录仪、无线视频传输设备及其供应链合规，促使厂商审查芯片来源，并削弱通过贴牌更换品牌规避限制的做法。

items.title: Wolves roam into Finnish villages after Google destroys 1,300 acres of forest for AI data centers
items.description: Wolves, who used to live in the forests recently cleared for Google data center development, are now roaming into Finnish villages nearby.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Google’s Finland country manager has apologized for unauthorized forest clearings near Muhos, which have turned 816 acres of forest into an expanse of mud. The American search and AI giant has also been told to cease work where it has cleared roughly 500 acres of forest, 55 miles southeast of the village of Otanmäki. Now The Guardian reports that wolves, who used to live in the forests, are roaming into villages neighboring these man-made muddy wastelands.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleLocal anger continues to simmer over the damage done to Finnish forests, as Google seems to have ridden roughshod over regulations in the hurry to build new AI data centers in Finland. However, the report suggests that it isn’t just environmentalists who have a beef with Google. Some families say wolves and other wild animals have entered the countryside villages. This would be a serious human safety concern.“We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” explained Anni Ranta, 53, whose family has lived in Otanmäki for generations. Ranta also fears the U.S.-owned data centers will make Finland an even juicier target for Russian aggression.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Finland is far from the first place targeted by AI data center developers to complain about environmental effects. This latest report also cites locals grumbling about construction/factory noise, streams turning brown, and rare birds being pushed out, among other unwanted side effects. We’ve seen similar concerns voiced across the U.S. and in other countries.Google’s flouting of environmental policy has been unprecedented and clear, a representative of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation (SLL) indicated to The Guardian. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) seems to agree, as it issued an order for Google to stop development near Muhos and Otanmäki. Nevertheless, a Google spokesperson was upbeat. “We will fully comply with LVV’s requests in this matter,” they said. “We look forward to maintaining an active, open dialogue with all authorities to strengthen our partnership with Finland and local organizations.” Google must be hoping the touted business benefits of the data centers will sway the government and/or regulators. items.titleZh: 谷歌为AI数据中心毁掉1300英亩森林后，狼群闯入芬兰村庄
items.descriptionZh:
谷歌在芬兰的AI数据中心项目因未经授权砍伐森林而引发监管与社区反弹。谷歌芬兰国家经理已就穆霍斯（Muhos）附近的森林清理道歉：约816英亩森林被推成泥地。芬兰许可与监督局（LVV）还要求谷歌停止在奥坦迈基村东南约55英里处已清理约500英亩森林的作业。此前，LVV已就穆霍斯和卡亚尼（奥坦迈基附近）的建设活动发出停工通知。芬兰自然保护协会（SLL）代表称，谷歌对环境政策的漠视“前所未有且明确”，LVV显然也持类似判断。

事件背景是AI算力需求激增推动数据中心扩张。AI数据中心需要大规模服务器集群、稳定电力与冷却系统，选址涉及土地、水资源、能源和社区影响；但报道未披露具体AI芯片、冷却架构或能效创新，争议核心是项目推进速度与生态监管之间的冲突。环境与社区副作用包括森林被毁、施工和设施噪音、溪流变褐、稀有鸟类被挤出栖息地。更直接的是，当地居民称狼等野生动物因森林消失而进入村庄，构成人身安全担忧。53岁的Anni Ranta表示，其家族世代居住在奥坦迈基，狼进入村庄是因为动物被迫离开森林；她还担心美国公司拥有的数据中心会使芬兰更容易成为俄罗斯攻击目标。反对者不仅是环保人士，也包括普通家庭。

谷歌发言人称将“完全遵守LVV在此事上的要求”，并期待与当局和当地组织保持积极、开放的对话。谷歌显然希望数据中心带来的商业利益能说服政府和监管者。报道还称，类似的环境副作用争议在美国和其他国家也出现过。相关报道提到，该项目因约420个足球场大小的芬兰森林被毁而受到调查。整体看，此案凸显AI基础设施快速扩张中的土地与生态合规风险：数据中心作为AI算力底座，其选址、许可和社区沟通与芯片性能同样影响项目可持续性；若监管收紧或社区反对升级，可能拖延建设进度、增加合规成本，并影响科技公司在欧洲的AI基础设施布局。

items.title: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future
items.description: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment.  The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with […]
items.content: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people. “If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.” Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally. Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity. For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. He said aspiring AI programmers should understand the technology’s principles, strengths and weaknesses, combining technical knowledge with the ability to work effectively with AI. “I envy being 18 years old today… because the world is changing so rapidly, and there’s a complete reset because of technology.” The Infrastructure Layer Is Scaling The visits coincided with a signing ceremony marking Firebird’s investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan, held at the presidential palace. Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships. Firebird cofounder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian attended the signing ceremony at the Akorda Presidential Palace alongside government officials. “What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan’s AI future,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-Founder and CEO of Firebird. “President Tokayev’s vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We’re building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan’s talent and ideas to reach the world.” Kazakhtelecom, the nation’s largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. Next year, the company plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in the Data Center Valley, along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region, serving diverse workloads with infrastructure that enterprises, developers and institutions can use at scale. An Honorary Black Belt for Huang Later that day, also at the Akorda Presidential Palace, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented Huang with an honorary black belt in Judo. The belt, embroidered in gold stitching, was a special thanks from President Tokayev for Huang’s support of Kazakhstan’s AI ambition and for leadership aligned with the spirit and rigor of the martial art. At the end of their meeting President Tokayev had another honor for Huang, presenting him with the Order of Dostyk, First Class, for Huang’s contribution to the development of artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan. Dostyk means friendship and the Order honors peace, friendship and cooperation. AI-Native Companies Scale With Compute And that development is accelerating. The nation’s AI-native companies are also building out their compute capacity — and the applications that run atop them. Higgsfield is expanding its AI infrastructure with NVIDIA Vera Rubin running on cloud service providers, giving the company additional capacity as models, products and customer demand for its generative media applications grow. inDrive and Pony.ai are also collaborating to explore robotaxi services in Kazakhstan, with Astana as the first deployment city. The companies will assess the feasibility of bringing Pony.ai’s seventh-generation robotaxis to the inDrive app, supported by NVIDIA AI infrastructure, built on the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute platform with the NVIDIA Halos safety system. More local capacity gives developers and companies room to train, fine-tune and serve increasingly capable models. Successful applications, in turn, create demand for more compute. Kazakhstan’s AI opportunity isn’t defined by GPU counts alone. Connecting that infrastructure with developers, universities, startups and industries can turn accelerated computing into useful applications. That was at the core of the discussion the NVIDIA team had with hundreds of developers from across Kazakhstan during a reception later in the evening. The gathering in this self-proclaimed AI nation was inspiring because of the ideas shared, the clear drive to build and a collective ambition to share it with the world. Today’s announcements represent different layers of the AI stack in Kazakhstan— infrastructure deployment, access to compute and AI-native product development — where the AI foundation is reaching new scale. items.titleZh: 哈萨克斯坦扩展算力，布局人工智能未来
items.descriptionZh:
哈萨克斯坦的人工智能生态正从基础设施规划转向实际部署，变化覆盖从算力基础设施、模型到应用的全栈。英伟达创始人兼CEO黄仁勋10月23日访问阿斯塔纳，在总统府会见总统托卡耶夫，并与副总理兼人工智能和数字发展部长扎斯兰·马迪耶夫在Alem.AI进行公开对话。这一系列动态表明，哈萨克斯坦正在增加加速计算供给，同时扩大对上层AI应用的需求。

在Alem.AI的对话中，马迪耶夫表示哈萨克斯坦希望建设反映本国语言和文化的AI，正在推进哈萨克语模型，使AI能够理解哈萨克语并捕捉文化语境和文化特征。黄仁勋提出，哈萨克斯坦可以把能源资源转化为AI生产的基础，形成新型出口：“未来不只是出口能源，而是把能源转化为智能并出口智能。”他强调本地数据是国家的自然资源，体现国家的文化、历史和价值观，“属于你们自己”。双方还讨论物理AI，马迪耶夫认为工厂、矿山、农业、交通和物流是潜在发展方向，并询问如何把哈萨克斯坦打造成机器人和物理系统模型训练的枢纽。黄仁勋称这一想法“非常棒”，认为物理AI可改造从采矿、矿物加工到农业的行业，并表示AI和机器人能帮助人们做更多事情，而雄心将决定抓住机会的程度。

对话还涉及AI安全。黄仁勋表示技术必须负责任地开发和部署，并介绍英伟达OpenShell可通过限制AI智能体对文件和工具的访问、监控其活动来约束AI智能体。对于进入快速变化领域的年轻人，他建议理解AI如何工作，而不只是会使用AI，掌握技术原理、优势和局限，并把技术知识与有效使用AI的能力结合起来。活动期间宣布英伟达投资哈萨克斯坦创立的初创公司Higgsfield AI，黄仁勋称“首先和最终都是投资人，而不是投资公司”，并称赞创始人有远见、努力参与全球竞争。

基础设施层面同步扩张。Firebird与哈萨克斯坦政府在总统府签署投资协议。继在亚美尼亚建设首个AI工厂后，Firebird进入哈萨克斯坦，并获得美国出口许可，可采购45,000块英伟达Grace Blackwell GPU。第一阶段与哈萨克斯坦电信在Data Center Valley建设，目标2027年第三季度商业启动；规划中的第二阶段将使Firebird在哈萨克斯坦的潜在AI基础设施总容量达到约500兆瓦。Firebird还计划设立Firebird Labs Kazakhstan，通过资金、算力获取和研究合作支持本地AI初创企业、研究和人才培养。Firebird联合创始人兼CEO拉兹米格·霍瓦吉米安表示，这一项目从180天前的一个想法成长为对哈萨克斯坦AI未来的重大投资，总统的愿景让他们有信心建设更大规模的基础设施，让哈萨克斯坦的人才和创意走向世界。

哈萨克斯坦电信已在该国阿斯塔纳和阿拉木图部署400块英伟达H200和480块英伟达B300 GPU。明年，该公司计划在Data Center Valley部署超过1,000块GPU，并在埃基巴斯图兹地区部署超过1,000块英伟达Vera Rubin GPU，以服务企业、开发者和机构可规模化使用的多样化工作负载。参数上，Firebird的45,000块Grace Blackwell GPU和约500兆瓦潜在容量，与哈萨克斯坦电信当前约880块H200/B300及明年超过2,000块新增GPU形成从国家级AI工厂到电信运营商算力底座的层次；H200/B300代表当前部署能力，Vera Rubin则指向下一代平台扩容。

AI原生公司也在借助算力扩展应用。Higgsfield正通过云服务商上的英伟达Vera Rubin扩展AI基础设施，以满足其生成式媒体应用在模型、产品和客户需求增长下的额外容量。inDrive与Pony.ai合作探索在哈萨克斯坦提供Robotaxi服务，阿斯塔纳为首个部署城市；双方将评估把Pony.ai第七代Robotaxi接入inDrive应用的可行性，依托英伟达AI基础设施，基于英伟达Hyperion传感器与计算平台及Halos安全系统。更多本地算力为开发者和企业训练、微调和服务更强模型提供空间，成功应用又创造更多算力需求，形成“算力—模型—应用”的飞轮。

当天晚些时候，托卡耶夫总统在总统府授予黄仁勋柔道荣誉黑带，以感谢其对哈萨克斯坦AI雄心的支持，并授予“Dostyk”一级勋章，表彰其对哈萨克斯坦人工智能发展的贡献。“Dostyk”意为友谊，该勋章褒奖和平、友谊与合作。整体来看，哈萨克斯坦的AI机会不只是GPU数量，而在于把加速计算基础设施与开发者、大学、初创企业和产业连接起来，将算力转化为有用应用。此次宣布覆盖基础设施部署、算力获取和AI原生产品开发等AI栈不同层面，显示哈萨克斯坦的AI基础正达到新规模，并可能把能源、数据和人才优势转化为语言模型、物理AI、生成式媒体和自动驾驶等场景的产业能力。

history.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia
history.description: Amazon has ditched its plans to build four new data centers in Loudoun County, Northern Virginia, following an outcry from local residents and officials. The land will now be repurposed for mixed and residential use.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Amazon will no longer build four new data centers on the site of the George Washington University's campus in Loudoun County, just outside of D.C., and will instead repurpose the majority of the 122-acre space for mixed-use and residential development following significant pushback from the local community. It will also donate 25 acres of the property to Loudoun County to be used for a community arts center and new recreational facility. On top of all that, it'll even give $5 million to the county's fund for housing, reports The Washington Post.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedThat's quite the turnaround compared to plans to build in a county that is already dubbed "Data Center Alley" because it has the largest concentration of data centers on the planet. But residents' concerns about the noise generated by such data centers and the incredible amount of power that they require to function have seen the county's approach to new data center buildouts change of late. Amazon first submitted its proposal to build the new facilities in July, and Loudoun County Board of Supervisors Chair Phyllis J. Randall and Amazon met in September, where it was put to the company that it may be better to find an alternative use for the land.Josh Weissman, Amazon’s vice president in charge of data center development, said the company had jumped at the chance to purchase the former university campus when the opportunity arose, but added that the company considered the county’s “pointed concerns about data center development at this particular site.” Weissman added that “While we see the property’s legal development potential differently than the County does, we concluded that the best outcome for all is to come together on a shared vision for this campus rather than engage in costly litigation.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The building of new data centers has always been a necessity given our growing use of cloud-based services and storage systems. But the recent boom in AI use has seen demand for additional, and larger, facilities ratcheted up to new levels. But with that demand comes opposition, with local communities wary of the impact these mammoth facilities can have on the areas in which they live, including spikes in the price of electricity. Officials have begun taking steps to try to grease the wheels of data center construction. Just days before this news broke, President Donald Trump called for data center builders and AI hyperscalers to pay local communities a dividend amid energy-related price increases. In a social media post, Trump went on to say that data centers would be required not only to make their own electricity but also to give or sell excess energy back to the local community. Water shortages and deforestation have also become key issues affecting the communities in which data centers are being placed.Back in Loudoun County, officials pointed to what could be achieved when choosing dialog over confrontation. “By choosing dialogue over reflexive disagreement, Loudoun County and Amazon created an opportunity for the County,” Randall reportedly said via statement. “This agreement provides new places for our Loudoun residents to gather, create, and play. history.titleZh: 亚马逊迫于当地对AI数据中心的反对，放弃在北弗吉尼亚新建四座设施的计划
history.descriptionZh:
亚马逊已决定不再在乔治·华盛顿大学位于弗吉尼亚州劳登县、华盛顿特区近郊的校园地块上建设四座新数据中心，而是将122英亩土地的大部分改作混合用途和住宅开发。这一转向发生在地当地社区强烈反对之后。亚马逊还将向劳登县捐赠25英亩土地，用于建设社区艺术中心和新的休闲设施，并向该县住房基金捐款500万美元。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，这与此前在“数据中心巷”继续扩张的计划形成明显反差——劳登县因拥有全球最大规模的数据中心集群而被称为“数据中心巷”，但居民对数据中心噪音和巨大耗电量的担忧，已促使该县对新数据中心建设采取更审慎态度。

事件时间线显示，亚马逊于7月首次提交建设新数据中心的提案，9月与劳登县监事会主席菲利斯·J·兰德尔会面，县方提出为该地块寻找替代用途可能更合适。亚马逊数据中心开发副总裁乔什·韦斯曼表示，公司当初抓住机会购买这处前大学校园地块，但也考虑了县方对“这一特定地点数据中心开发”的尖锐关切。他说，尽管亚马逊与县方对该地块的法律开发潜力看法不同，但公司认为共同形成校园愿景比陷入代价高昂的诉讼更符合各方利益。

从技术需求背景看，云服务和存储系统持续增长，使新建数据中心长期具有必要性；而近期AI应用爆发进一步推高了对更大规模设施的需求。数据中心为AI训练、推理和云服务提供算力、存储与网络，需要持续供电和冷却，并产生噪音，因此其选址越来越受电力、水资源和社区承受能力约束。原文未披露这四座数据中心原计划的IT负载、PUE、用水量等具体性能参数，但协议中的关键“参数”包括：不再建设四座数据中心、122英亩地块大部分改为混合用途和住宅、捐赠25英亩公共设施用地、500万美元住房基金。这反映出数据中心开发模式的一种调整：不再只强调土地和法律开发权，而是通过土地捐赠、住房基金和公共设施等社区收益包换取社会许可，并以协商替代诉讼。

围绕数据中心的反对还涉及电价上涨、水资源短缺和森林砍伐等问题。就在这一消息传出前几天，美国总统特朗普呼吁数据中心建设者和AI超大规模企业向当地社区支付“红利”，并要求数据中心自行发电，并将多余电力赠送或出售给当地社区。劳登县官员则强调对话优于对抗。兰德尔表示，通过选择对话而非条件反射式反对，劳登县和亚马逊为该县创造了机会；协议将为居民提供聚会、创作和活动的场所，更重要的是为工薪家庭提供更多可负担住房。

这一案例的技术影响不在芯片或服务器本身，而在AI基础设施扩张的落地方式：随着AI数据中心功率密度和总用电规模上升，项目能否推进越来越取决于电力配套、噪音控制、用水约束和社区利益共享。未来超大规模数据中心选址可能更早引入社区沟通，并配套自发电、余电回馈、公共设施和住房基金等机制。应用场景上，这既关系到亚马逊云服务和AI算力的长期扩容，也为地方政府与数据中心运营商处理选址冲突提供了一个“协商换社区收益”的样本。

history.title: Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network
history.description: A security firm has been able to identify 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 AI chips running inside a China Telecom network, but it's unclear where the export-barred components are physically located.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Lava, an Israeli security firm, says that it has been able to identify 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips within the network of China Telecom, a state-owned company that provides telecommunications services within the country. These same chips have already been barred from export by U.S. export controls, a report by The Information notes, which begs the question of how they have turned up in a Chinese data center. Such chips can only be sold to whitelisted buyers who agree not to export them to sanctioned parties, including those in China.However, banning companies from buying Nvidia's high-performance GPUs and AI data center chips hasn't always worked. In 2025, it was reported that Chinese companies smuggled $1 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips into the country in three months. At the time, the B200 chips were the most sought-after, but some distributors were already gearing up to sell B300-series chips when they became available.While the latest finding shows that the proliferation of export-controlled chips into China continues to be an issue, Nvidia has downplayed the report but didn't deny the findings. "Governments, researchers, and media have all found insignificant diversion of controlled US products, less than one half of one percent in recent court cases — a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has," an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. "With tens of millions of GPUs in service in approved countries, this report again demonstrates that smuggling is a nonfactor, blocked by governments on both sides of the globe."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: It's unknown how B300 chips found their way into China Telecom's server racks, nor can Lava confirm exactly where within the company's network they are located. But they are there, with Lava identifying them via Nvidia's own DCGM Exporter tool. The software can be installed by data center operators and is used to monitor server health and performance, and while designed for internal use, it can oftentimes be accessed beyond the data center's network. Oddly, it doesn't always require password authentication, either. Nvidia previously confirmed it was working on a tool that would allow its chips to be located, but it is yet to be released.It's easy to see why Chinese firms are keen to get their hands on the Blackwell Ultra B300. Announced in March of last year, the data center GPU is one of the most powerful on the planet, offering huge performance gains with 50% more memory and FP4 compute than the previous-generation B200. At the time, Nvidia touted that the chip was "built for the age of reasoning," while name-checking more sophisticated AI LLMs like DeepSeek R1. At the time of its announcement, the B300 was expected to ship by the end of 2025, and it didn't take long for it to become hot property. In August 2026, nine people were indicted in Taiwan over the illegal export of B300 GPUs to China. This came just days after Supermicro confirmed that it had fired several employees following an investigation into smuggling. The complicated smuggling process included the use of a Taiwanese server trading firm called Flying Tiget Tech — a firm with whitelisted status for GPU purchases. The company's A100 servers have tripled in price, despite being five years old, and can cost up to $82.,000. The ongoing crackdown on Nvidia chip smuggling has even seen some resort to retooling gaming GPUs to run AI workloads where possible. history.titleZh: 国有中国电信网络中发现非法英伟达Blackwell Ultra B300 GPU
history.descriptionZh:
以色列安全公司Lava称，其在中国电信的网络中识别出32颗英伟达Blackwell Ultra B300数据中心GPU。中国电信是中国国有电信服务提供商，而这些B300芯片属于美国出口管制禁止对华出口的高性能AI芯片。The Information报道称，这一发现引出了关键问题：受控芯片如何进入中国数据中心。按照美国管制规则，此类芯片只能出售给白名单买家，且买家须承诺不将其再出口至受制裁方，包括中国实体。英伟达方面淡化报告影响，但未否认Lava的发现。其发言人表示，政府、研究机构和媒体近期在法院案件中发现的受控美国产品转移“微不足道”，不到0.5%，相比中国已拥有的海量本土算力只是“沧海一粟”；在获批国家有数千万颗GPU在役，报告再次说明走私并非主要因素，且受到全球多国政府拦截。

Lava并未说明这些B300如何进入中国电信的服务器机架，也无法确认它们在中国电信网络中的具体位置，但表示芯片确实存在。识别方式是利用英伟达自有的DCGM Exporter工具。该软件由数据中心运营商安装，用于监控服务器健康状态和性能，原本面向内部使用，但经常可从数据中心网络外部访问，而且并不总是要求密码认证。英伟达此前确认正在开发一种可定位其芯片的工具，但尚未发布。这一发现也暴露了AI数据中心监控接口暴露带来的硬件部署信息泄露风险。

中国公司之所以热衷获取Blackwell Ultra B300，是因为该数据中心GPU是当前最强性能产品之一。它于去年3月发布，英伟达称其“为推理时代而构建”，并点名DeepSeek R1等更复杂的AI大模型。与上一代B200相比，B300的内存容量和FP4计算能力均提升50%。FP4是一种低精度浮点格式，可在AI推理中降低内存带宽和能耗、提高吞吐量；更大的内存则有助于承载更大模型、减少多卡通信开销。B300原预计2025年底出货，随后迅速成为抢手货。2026年8月，台湾九人因非法向中国出口B300 GPU被起诉；几天前，Supermicro在走私调查后确认解雇数名员工。报道称，复杂走私链条涉及一家名为Flying Tiget Tech的台湾服务器贸易公司，该公司拥有GPU采购白名单资格。

这一事件延续了受出口管制英伟达AI芯片持续流入中国的背景。2025年曾有报道称，中国公司在三个月内走私了价值10亿美元的英伟达AI芯片，当时B200最受欢迎，部分分销商已准备在B300上市后销售。英伟达芯片对AI数据中心至关重要，甚至旧款产品价格也大幅上涨：发布五年的A100服务器价格已上涨两倍，最高可达8.2万美元；在走私打击持续之际，还有人尝试改造游戏GPU用于AI工作负载。总体来看，B300现身中国电信网络说明，尽管美国出口管制和白名单机制已建立，但通过分销链、服务器集成和跨境贸易规避管制的风险仍然存在；同时，DCGM Exporter等运维工具的外部暴露也为追踪受控硬件提供了线索。该事件将影响美国出口管制有效性辩论、英伟达合规与供应链审查，以及运营商AI数据中心的安全配置实践。B300的主要应用场景包括大规模AI推理、运营商AI云服务和数据中心大模型部署。

history.title: FCC issues first bans under new chip-level rule
history.description: FCC bans a dashcam and wireless video transmitter produced by HiSilicon, a subsidiary of Huawei for containing an AI chip that advertises face detection algorithms.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The FCC recently imposed a new rule allowing it to ban devices based on the internal chips instead of basing bans on individual products or brands, thus closing the loophole of rebranded products with parts from Chinese manufacturers on US export restriction lists. Using this new rule, the FCC has banned two devices from being sold and marketed in the US for the first time: a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter. As reported by The Verge, these devices were banned due to the HiSilicon Smart Vision SoC (System on a Chip) they contain, which features built-in detection algorithms for faces. HiSilicon is a subsidiary of Huawei, and the firm and its subsidiaries are on the FCC’s Covered List of entities that pose a risk to US national security.The Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision is an SoC for surveillance and camera products. The SoC is meant to be used for things like vehicle dashcams and wireless CCTV systems; fully equipped with WiFi, Ethernet, video encoding chips, an Arm Cortex-A7, and an NPU (Neural Processing Unit) for AI features. The NPU is what the FCC is concerned about, explaining that it is a device that contains logic-bearing “smart” components produced by entities on the Covered List. (Image credit: HiSilicon)On the SoC’s data sheet, the Intelligent Video Engine (IVE) uses the NPU that runs a built-in dedicated multimodal large model and transformer feature acceleration. The transformer feature acceleration allows the AI model to understand the relationship between objects from one video frame to another, keeping “attention” between related objects: pets, faces, human figures, and parcels, as the data sheet advertises. For consumers, this potentially means the AI in a surveillance camera can understand whether it is your pet that is escaping, or an unknown person is stealing your parcel after understanding that it was placed by a courier worker.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, the FCC believes the logic-bearing AI in the SoC can do something much more nefarious, surveying US citizens and logging faces for foreign surveillance. Huawei already had a previous AI chip scandal, using shell companies to deceive TSMC into producing AI chips for them, going against the US’ request for TSMC to halt supplies to a list of Chinese customers; among other Huawei scandals leading to other product bans in the US. history.titleZh: FCC依据新芯片级规则首次发布禁令
history.descriptionZh:
美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）近期实施了一项新的设备准入规则，使其可以依据设备内部所用芯片，而非仅依据具体产品型号或品牌，来决定是否禁止相关设备进入美国市场。这一规则改变了此前监管主要针对整机产品或品牌的路径，重点堵住“重新贴牌”规避限制的漏洞：即使最终产品以不同品牌销售，只要其中包含来自美国出口限制名单或FCC“ Covered List”上中国厂商的部件，FCC仍可对设备实施禁售。借助这一新规，FCC首次禁止两款设备在美国销售和推广：一款行车记录仪和一款无线视频传输器。据The Verge报道，这两款产品被禁的原因是其内部使用了海思（HiSilicon）的Smart Vision系统级芯片（SoC），该芯片内置人脸检测算法。海思是华为子公司，而华为及其子公司被列入FCC的“Covered List”，该名单涵盖被认定对美国国家安全构成风险的实体。

涉事芯片型号为Hi3516CV610 UHD Smart Vision，定位面向监控和摄像类产品的SoC，目标应用包括车载行车记录仪和无线CCTV系统。该芯片集成WiFi、以太网、视频编码芯片、Arm Cortex-A7 CPU，以及用于AI功能的NPU（神经网络处理单元）。FCC主要担忧的正是其NPU及由此带来的“智能”逻辑处理能力。FCC解释称，这类设备包含由“Covered List”实体生产的、具备逻辑运算能力的智能组件。

根据该SoC的数据表，其智能视频引擎（IVE）利用NPU运行内置的专用多模态大模型，并支持Transformer特征加速。Transformer特征加速使AI模型能够理解不同视频帧中对象之间的关系，并在相关对象之间保持“注意力”，数据表宣传的对象包括宠物、人脸、人体和包裹。对消费者而言，这意味着监控摄像头中的AI有望区分具体场景：例如，是自家的宠物正在跑出去，还是陌生人正在偷走包裹，并且能够理解包裹是由快递员放置的。这类边缘AI视觉能力可提升车载记录、家庭和商业安防、无线视频传输等场景的智能分析体验。

不过，FCC认为，该SoC中具备逻辑运算能力的AI还可能被用于更敏感的目的，例如对美国公民进行监控、记录人脸信息并用于外国 surveillance。报道还提到，华为此前曾卷入AI芯片相关丑闻，被指利用空壳公司欺骗台积电为其生产AI芯片，违反美国要求台积电停止向一批中国客户供货的要求；此外还有其他华为相关事件导致其产品在美国被禁。需要指出的是，原文并未披露该芯片的具体算力、功耗、视频帧率、检测精度等量化性能参数，也没有给出与其他同类芯片的逐项对比数据。此次事件更重要的“对比”在于监管方式的变化：从此前针对具体产品/品牌的禁令，转向可依据内部芯片实施禁售，并且这是FCC首次依据该规则禁止设备。其影响可能延伸到美国市场的安防摄像头、行车记录仪、无线视频传输设备及其供应链合规，促使厂商审查芯片来源，并削弱通过贴牌更换品牌规避限制的做法。

history.title: Wolves roam into Finnish villages after Google destroys 1,300 acres of forest for AI data centers
history.description: Wolves, who used to live in the forests recently cleared for Google data center development, are now roaming into Finnish villages nearby.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Google’s Finland country manager has apologized for unauthorized forest clearings near Muhos, which have turned 816 acres of forest into an expanse of mud. The American search and AI giant has also been told to cease work where it has cleared roughly 500 acres of forest, 55 miles southeast of the village of Otanmäki. Now The Guardian reports that wolves, who used to live in the forests, are roaming into villages neighboring these man-made muddy wastelands.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleLocal anger continues to simmer over the damage done to Finnish forests, as Google seems to have ridden roughshod over regulations in the hurry to build new AI data centers in Finland. However, the report suggests that it isn’t just environmentalists who have a beef with Google. Some families say wolves and other wild animals have entered the countryside villages. This would be a serious human safety concern.“We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” explained Anni Ranta, 53, whose family has lived in Otanmäki for generations. Ranta also fears the U.S.-owned data centers will make Finland an even juicier target for Russian aggression.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Finland is far from the first place targeted by AI data center developers to complain about environmental effects. This latest report also cites locals grumbling about construction/factory noise, streams turning brown, and rare birds being pushed out, among other unwanted side effects. We’ve seen similar concerns voiced across the U.S. and in other countries.Google’s flouting of environmental policy has been unprecedented and clear, a representative of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation (SLL) indicated to The Guardian. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) seems to agree, as it issued an order for Google to stop development near Muhos and Otanmäki. Nevertheless, a Google spokesperson was upbeat. “We will fully comply with LVV’s requests in this matter,” they said. “We look forward to maintaining an active, open dialogue with all authorities to strengthen our partnership with Finland and local organizations.” Google must be hoping the touted business benefits of the data centers will sway the government and/or regulators. history.titleZh: 谷歌为AI数据中心毁掉1300英亩森林后，狼群闯入芬兰村庄
history.descriptionZh:
谷歌在芬兰的AI数据中心项目因未经授权砍伐森林而引发监管与社区反弹。谷歌芬兰国家经理已就穆霍斯（Muhos）附近的森林清理道歉：约816英亩森林被推成泥地。芬兰许可与监督局（LVV）还要求谷歌停止在奥坦迈基村东南约55英里处已清理约500英亩森林的作业。此前，LVV已就穆霍斯和卡亚尼（奥坦迈基附近）的建设活动发出停工通知。芬兰自然保护协会（SLL）代表称，谷歌对环境政策的漠视“前所未有且明确”，LVV显然也持类似判断。

事件背景是AI算力需求激增推动数据中心扩张。AI数据中心需要大规模服务器集群、稳定电力与冷却系统，选址涉及土地、水资源、能源和社区影响；但报道未披露具体AI芯片、冷却架构或能效创新，争议核心是项目推进速度与生态监管之间的冲突。环境与社区副作用包括森林被毁、施工和设施噪音、溪流变褐、稀有鸟类被挤出栖息地。更直接的是，当地居民称狼等野生动物因森林消失而进入村庄，构成人身安全担忧。53岁的Anni Ranta表示，其家族世代居住在奥坦迈基，狼进入村庄是因为动物被迫离开森林；她还担心美国公司拥有的数据中心会使芬兰更容易成为俄罗斯攻击目标。反对者不仅是环保人士，也包括普通家庭。

谷歌发言人称将“完全遵守LVV在此事上的要求”，并期待与当局和当地组织保持积极、开放的对话。谷歌显然希望数据中心带来的商业利益能说服政府和监管者。报道还称，类似的环境副作用争议在美国和其他国家也出现过。相关报道提到，该项目因约420个足球场大小的芬兰森林被毁而受到调查。整体看，此案凸显AI基础设施快速扩张中的土地与生态合规风险：数据中心作为AI算力底座，其选址、许可和社区沟通与芯片性能同样影响项目可持续性；若监管收紧或社区反对升级，可能拖延建设进度、增加合规成本，并影响科技公司在欧洲的AI基础设施布局。

history.title: Kazakhstan Expands Compute for Its AI Future
history.description: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment.  The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. history.content: Kazakhstan’s AI ecosystem is moving from infrastructure plans to deployment. The shift is visible across the full AI stack — from infrastructure to models to applications. The announcements below — coinciding with a visit to Astana by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang — point to the nation’s increasing supply of accelerated computing, along with its growing demand for what comes next. On Friday, Oct. 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda Presidential Palace and joining Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev — Kazakhstan’s minister of AI and digital development — for a public fireside chat at the Alem.AI program. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Jensen Huang and Kazakhstan’s AI Minister Speak at Alem.AI In their fireside chat at Alem.AI, Kazakhstan’s international center for artificial intelligence, Madiyev and Huang discussed the country’s push to become an AI nation — building the energy and computing infrastructure to support homegrown AI and applying it across the economy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan wants AI that reflects its language and culture. “We want AI that understands and speaks Kazakh and captures cultural contexts and cultural specifics,” he said, describing the country’s work on Kazakh-language models. Huang said Kazakhstan could turn its energy resources into a foundation for AI production — and a new kind of export. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” he said. He also argued that local data is central to that ambition: it embodies a country’s culture, history and values. “Your country’s data is your natural resource. It belongs to you.” The conversation also turned to physical AI. Madiyev pointed to Kazakhstan’s factories, mines, agriculture, transport and logistics as potential areas for development, asking how the country could become a hub for training models for robots and other physical systems. Huang called the idea “fantastic,” saying physical AI could transform industries from mining and mineral processing to agriculture. Huang said AI and robotics can help people do more, but ambition will shape how fully they seize that opportunity. He applied the idea to Kazakhstan, saying AI could help lift the country and its people. “If you have ambition, and I believe you do, AI will lift your nation,” Huang said. “AI will lift your people.” Huang also praised the founders of Higgsfield AI, the Kazakhstan-founded startup, and it was announced NVIDIA is making an investment into the startup during the event. “The first thing and the last thing is you invest in people, not companies,” he said, describing the founders as visionary and pointing to their effort to compete globally. Asked about AI security, Huang said the technology must be developed and deployed responsibly. He described NVIDIA’s OpenShell as a way to contain AI agents by limiting their access to files and tools and monitoring their activity. For young people entering a fast-changing field, Huang recommended learning how AI works — not just how to use it. He said aspiring AI programmers should understand the technology’s principles, strengths and weaknesses, combining technical knowledge with the ability to work effectively with AI. “I envy being 18 years old today… because the world is changing so rapidly, and there’s a complete reset because of technology.” The Infrastructure Layer Is Scaling The visits coincided with a signing ceremony marking Firebird’s investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan, held at the presidential palace. Building on its first AI factory in Armenia, Firebird is expanding into Kazakhstan, where it has secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. A planned second phase would bring Firebird’s total potential AI infrastructure capacity in Kazakhstan to approximately 500 megawatts. Firebird also plans to establish Firebird Labs Kazakhstan to support local AI startups, research and talent development through funding, access to compute and research partnerships. Firebird cofounder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian attended the signing ceremony at the Akorda Presidential Palace alongside government officials. “What began as a seed of an idea 180 days ago has grown into a major investment in Kazakhstan’s AI future,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-Founder and CEO of Firebird. “President Tokayev’s vision gave us the confidence to think bigger about what we can build together. With Jensen Huang here today, that ambition feels more tangible than ever. We’re building the infrastructure for Kazakhstan’s talent and ideas to reach the world.” Kazakhtelecom, the nation’s largest telecommunications company, has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. Next year, the company plans to deploy more than 1,000 GPUs in the Data Center Valley, along with more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region, serving diverse workloads with infrastructure that enterprises, developers and institutions can use at scale. An Honorary Black Belt for Huang Later that day, also at the Akorda Presidential Palace, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented Huang with an honorary black belt in Judo. The belt, embroidered in gold stitching, was a special thanks from President Tokayev for Huang’s support of Kazakhstan’s AI ambition and for leadership aligned with the spirit and rigor of the martial art. At the end of their meeting President Tokayev had another honor for Huang, presenting him with the Order of Dostyk, First Class, for Huang’s contribution to the development of artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan. Dostyk means friendship and the Order honors peace, friendship and cooperation. AI-Native Companies Scale With Compute And that development is accelerating. The nation’s AI-native companies are also building out their compute capacity — and the applications that run atop them. Higgsfield is expanding its AI infrastructure with NVIDIA Vera Rubin running on cloud service providers, giving the company additional capacity as models, products and customer demand for its generative media applications grow. inDrive and Pony.ai are also collaborating to explore robotaxi services in Kazakhstan, with Astana as the first deployment city. The companies will assess the feasibility of bringing Pony.ai’s seventh-generation robotaxis to the inDrive app, supported by NVIDIA AI infrastructure, built on the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute platform with the NVIDIA Halos safety system. More local capacity gives developers and companies room to train, fine-tune and serve increasingly capable models. Successful applications, in turn, create demand for more compute. Kazakhstan’s AI opportunity isn’t defined by GPU counts alone. Connecting that infrastructure with developers, universities, startups and industries can turn accelerated computing into useful applications. That was at the core of the discussion the NVIDIA team had with hundreds of developers from across Kazakhstan during a reception later in the evening. The gathering in this self-proclaimed AI nation was inspiring because of the ideas shared, the clear drive to build and a collective ambition to share it with the world. Today’s announcements represent different layers of the AI stack in Kazakhstan— infrastructure deployment, access to compute and AI-native product development — where the AI foundation is reaching new scale. history.titleZh: 哈萨克斯坦扩展算力，布局人工智能未来
history.descriptionZh:
哈萨克斯坦的人工智能生态正从基础设施规划转向实际部署，变化覆盖从算力基础设施、模型到应用的全栈。英伟达创始人兼CEO黄仁勋10月23日访问阿斯塔纳，在总统府会见总统托卡耶夫，并与副总理兼人工智能和数字发展部长扎斯兰·马迪耶夫在Alem.AI进行公开对话。这一系列动态表明，哈萨克斯坦正在增加加速计算供给，同时扩大对上层AI应用的需求。

在Alem.AI的对话中，马迪耶夫表示哈萨克斯坦希望建设反映本国语言和文化的AI，正在推进哈萨克语模型，使AI能够理解哈萨克语并捕捉文化语境和文化特征。黄仁勋提出，哈萨克斯坦可以把能源资源转化为AI生产的基础，形成新型出口：“未来不只是出口能源，而是把能源转化为智能并出口智能。”他强调本地数据是国家的自然资源，体现国家的文化、历史和价值观，“属于你们自己”。双方还讨论物理AI，马迪耶夫认为工厂、矿山、农业、交通和物流是潜在发展方向，并询问如何把哈萨克斯坦打造成机器人和物理系统模型训练的枢纽。黄仁勋称这一想法“非常棒”，认为物理AI可改造从采矿、矿物加工到农业的行业，并表示AI和机器人能帮助人们做更多事情，而雄心将决定抓住机会的程度。

对话还涉及AI安全。黄仁勋表示技术必须负责任地开发和部署，并介绍英伟达OpenShell可通过限制AI智能体对文件和工具的访问、监控其活动来约束AI智能体。对于进入快速变化领域的年轻人，他建议理解AI如何工作，而不只是会使用AI，掌握技术原理、优势和局限，并把技术知识与有效使用AI的能力结合起来。活动期间宣布英伟达投资哈萨克斯坦创立的初创公司Higgsfield AI，黄仁勋称“首先和最终都是投资人，而不是投资公司”，并称赞创始人有远见、努力参与全球竞争。

基础设施层面同步扩张。Firebird与哈萨克斯坦政府在总统府签署投资协议。继在亚美尼亚建设首个AI工厂后，Firebird进入哈萨克斯坦，并获得美国出口许可，可采购45,000块英伟达Grace Blackwell GPU。第一阶段与哈萨克斯坦电信在Data Center Valley建设，目标2027年第三季度商业启动；规划中的第二阶段将使Firebird在哈萨克斯坦的潜在AI基础设施总容量达到约500兆瓦。Firebird还计划设立Firebird Labs Kazakhstan，通过资金、算力获取和研究合作支持本地AI初创企业、研究和人才培养。Firebird联合创始人兼CEO拉兹米格·霍瓦吉米安表示，这一项目从180天前的一个想法成长为对哈萨克斯坦AI未来的重大投资，总统的愿景让他们有信心建设更大规模的基础设施，让哈萨克斯坦的人才和创意走向世界。

哈萨克斯坦电信已在该国阿斯塔纳和阿拉木图部署400块英伟达H200和480块英伟达B300 GPU。明年，该公司计划在Data Center Valley部署超过1,000块GPU，并在埃基巴斯图兹地区部署超过1,000块英伟达Vera Rubin GPU，以服务企业、开发者和机构可规模化使用的多样化工作负载。参数上，Firebird的45,000块Grace Blackwell GPU和约500兆瓦潜在容量，与哈萨克斯坦电信当前约880块H200/B300及明年超过2,000块新增GPU形成从国家级AI工厂到电信运营商算力底座的层次；H200/B300代表当前部署能力，Vera Rubin则指向下一代平台扩容。

AI原生公司也在借助算力扩展应用。Higgsfield正通过云服务商上的英伟达Vera Rubin扩展AI基础设施，以满足其生成式媒体应用在模型、产品和客户需求增长下的额外容量。inDrive与Pony.ai合作探索在哈萨克斯坦提供Robotaxi服务，阿斯塔纳为首个部署城市；双方将评估把Pony.ai第七代Robotaxi接入inDrive应用的可行性，依托英伟达AI基础设施，基于英伟达Hyperion传感器与计算平台及Halos安全系统。更多本地算力为开发者和企业训练、微调和服务更强模型提供空间，成功应用又创造更多算力需求，形成“算力—模型—应用”的飞轮。

当天晚些时候，托卡耶夫总统在总统府授予黄仁勋柔道荣誉黑带，以感谢其对哈萨克斯坦AI雄心的支持，并授予“Dostyk”一级勋章，表彰其对哈萨克斯坦人工智能发展的贡献。“Dostyk”意为友谊，该勋章褒奖和平、友谊与合作。整体来看，哈萨克斯坦的AI机会不只是GPU数量，而在于把加速计算基础设施与开发者、大学、初创企业和产业连接起来，将算力转化为有用应用。此次宣布覆盖基础设施部署、算力获取和AI原生产品开发等AI栈不同层面，显示哈萨克斯坦的AI基础正达到新规模，并可能把能源、数据和人才优势转化为语言模型、物理AI、生成式媒体和自动驾驶等场景的产业能力。
